steps.what: Sum costs and revenue of the agreements.
Flag an agreement below the margin rule.
Evaluate continued profitability of the agreement.

tasks.design: Cost and revenue of each agreement are summed in {BI} from the {ERP}. A margin rule flags a weak agreement. The agent evaluates whether it should continue and signs that decision. The rule does not close an agreement by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Profit was a side sheet rebuilt when someone asked, so a weak agreement could run for months.
tasks.enabler_now: Cost, revenue and a margin threshold are arithmetic. Continuing the agreement is not.
tasks.still_hard: A client relationship can justify a thin margin, and only the agent can say so.
tasks.human_edge: The agent decides which agreement continues. The flag only shows the arithmetic.

ambition.what: Look at every agreement under the margin rule each month, including small ones that used to be ignored.

tasks.altitude: The agent stops rebuilding the sum and still decides which agreement stays.

reach.task: see which mandate earns below the fee rule
reach.learn: which shortfall is arithmetic and which mandate a person may keep

evidence.claim: Margin on an agreement is a sum and a threshold. The job digest puts that kind of check with code, and the decision with the person.
The job digest says call recording and scoring of sellers need works-council consent. This task adds neither.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The task evaluates agreements already in force. Negotiating a new price is another task.

Fields: agreement id, cost, revenue, margin, threshold. Cost and revenue come from the {ERP}. The threshold is a number the desk sets. The decision text is the agent's. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The ledger already holds cost and revenue. The build sums them and flags the threshold. It does not add a second ledger.
The decision version is signed. The rule cannot close the agreement. No seller score is stored.
unknowns: What margin the desk treats as too thin.
Whether cost includes a share of the desk or only direct cost.
research_questions: What share of agreements is below the threshold?
How often does the agent keep one anyway?

already_counted.description: The agent still decides which agreement continues.

incremental.description: Keep the margin threshold and the cost map current.

approvals.approved_version: margin-decision v1: agreement-id, margin, threshold, decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If cost is incomplete in the ledger, the flag is noise and the agent still rebuilds the sum for the agreements that matter.

steps.what: Prepare the sheet for the trust or the service.
Sell trusts, investments or check processing services.
Record the service the client accepted.

tasks.design: A one-page sheet in {DOCS} states the trust, the investment or the processing service and its price from the {CRM}. The agent sells it in the meeting. The record of what the client accepted is signed. The sheet is not the sale, and it does not speak for the agent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The service was described from memory, so the price on the sheet and the price in the meeting could differ.
tasks.enabler_now: The service name and the price are fields. The conversation that sells them is not.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this client should take the service is the sale, and a sheet cannot close it.
tasks.human_edge: The agent makes the sale and signs only what the client accepted.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays the work. The sheet and the acceptance record stop the price from drifting.

reach.task: sell a service from a one-page sheet
reach.learn: which line the client must accept before it is a sale

evidence.claim: A service sheet is a template. The job digest leaves the sale with the person.

The job digest says securities advice stays with the person, and advising staff need a diploma. A draft is not the advice. Selling a trust is not consumer-credit scoring, which is the only credit case the job digest marks as high-risk.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The task is the sale of a service in a meeting. Opening the product afterwards is another task.

Fields: service id, price, client id, accepted yes/no. Price comes from the service record. The agent marks accepted only after the client says so. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The {CRM} already lists the services. The build prints the sheet from those fields. It does not add a second catalogue.
The acceptance version is signed. Any edit voids it. No seller score is stored.
unknowns: Which of these services the desk is allowed to sell.
Whether acceptance must be followed by a signed form the same day.
research_questions: What share of these sales is a meeting rather than a call?
How often does the spoken price differ from the sheet?

already_counted.description: The agent still sells in the meeting.
The agent still records the acceptance.

incremental.description: Keep the service sheet headings and prices current.

approvals.approved_version: service-sale v1: client-id, service-id, price, accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the sale is still the meeting, the sheet saves the hunt for the price and not the conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Set out the last price and the open clause.
Negotiate prices or contracts with the counterparty.
Mark the negotiated version of the contract.

tasks.design: The last price and the open clause are on one {CLM} screen. The agent negotiates prices or contracts with the counterparty. The negotiated version is marked and signed before it is treated as the contract. A draft clause is not an agreement.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last price sat in a thread, so the negotiation started from two different numbers.
tasks.enabler_now: Showing the last signed price beside the open clause is a record. Agreeing a new one is not.
tasks.still_hard: The concession, the relationship and the walk-away stay in the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The agent negotiates and marks only the version that was agreed. A clause comparison does not close the deal.
tasks.altitude: The negotiation stays the work. The change is one screen for the last price and a marked version afterwards.

reach.task: negotiate a fee against the last signed mandate
reach.learn: which clause change voids the previous version

evidence.claim: Putting the last price and the open clause on one screen is a record. The job digest leaves negotiation with the person.
The job digest says call recording and scoring of sellers need works-council consent. This task adds neither.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The task is the negotiation. Sending a finished contract for signature may be a later step outside this task if a separate signer is required.

Fields: contract id, last price, open clause id, proposed price, proposed text. Last price comes from the signed version. The agent types the proposed text. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The contract record already stores versions. The build shows the last one. It does not add a second contract system.
Marking the version is the agent's signature. Any later edit voids it. No seller score is stored.
unknowns: Whether the counterparty is a client, a venue or another firm.
Who else must sign after the agent marks the version.
research_questions: What share of negotiations changes the price rather than a clause?
How often is a marked version reopened the same week?

already_counted.description: The agent still marks the version.

incremental.description: Keep the clause list and the version rule current.

approvals.approved_version: negotiated v1: contract-id, price, clause-ids, marked-date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the negotiation is still a long meeting, the screen saves the search for the last price and not the bargaining.

steps.what: Check the request before it is sent.
Send the approved request to the companies.
Read the quotations that come back.

loop.input: The reply and the instrument ids on the request.
loop.output: A price line that names an instrument on the request.
loop.check: Drop a line with no instrument id, and drop a price that is not a number.
loop.stop: If more than three lines fail, stop and leave the reply for the agent.
loop.why_not_simpler: Replies are free text. A fixed column map misses a sentence price and still needs the agent when the line is wrong.

tasks.design: The quotation request is built from the instrument list in the {CRM}: instrument, size and the date a reply is needed. The agent checks it. Only that version is sent to the companies. Replies are read back against the same list before a price is used. A price that does not match an instrument is not kept.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were typed one by one, and a reply was compared by eye to a list that had already changed.
tasks.enabler_now: The request is a list of instruments. Sending one approved version, and keeping only reply lines that name those instruments, is a check.
tasks.still_hard: Which company's price to accept is a later decision, and a reply can hide a condition in a sentence.
tasks.human_edge: The agent approves the request and still reads a reply the check cannot parse.

ambition.what: Send a checked quotation request for a small list as well, not only when the list is long enough to type by hand.

tasks.altitude: The agent stops retyping the same request and still decides what is sent and which reply to trust.

reach.task: request a rate from a supplier for a named trip
reach.learn: which field must match the request before a reply price is kept

evidence.claim: The job digest treats cost sums and price requests as rules on a rate card. A missing field goes back to the agent. No model sets the price.
Sending a price request is an external message the agent approves. It is not advice to a client, and it stores no seller score.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The task prepares and sends the request and reads the reply. Accepting a price into an order is another task.

Fields: instrument id, size, reply-by date, company id, price. The instrument list is the agent's. A reply line with no instrument id is dropped. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: Mail already reaches the companies. The build fills the request from the list and blocks a send of an unchecked version.
Any edit to the request voids the approval. A reply is not an order.
unknowns: Which companies are on the list for this market.
Whether replies arrive as a table or as prose.
research_questions: What share of requests is a repeat of the same instrument list?
How often is a reply missing a price?

already_counted.description: The agent still checks the request.
The agent still reads the replies the check cannot parse.

incremental.description: Keep the company list and the instrument list current.

approvals.approved_version: rfq v1: instrument-ids, sizes, reply-by, company-ids
rfq v1: instrument-ids, sizes, reply-by, company-ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If replies are prose and the list changes every time, the agent still writes most requests and the saving is the send of a stable list.

role.altitude: The agent keeps the sale, the negotiation and the decision to continue an agreement. Margin sums and quotation requests are prepared first.
reach: Insurance sales agent: sell a service in a meeting and record only what the client accepted.
Travel agent: send a price request that matches the trip, and read the reply before using it.
skills_to_grow: Tell a margin rule from a reason to keep an unprofitable agreement.
Mark the negotiated version so a later edit is obvious.
role.ambitious_version: Every agreement is checked against its margin, and a small quotation request goes out only in the version the agent signed.
